title: Debug a Local Web App
goal: Use the runtime mental models from this track to diagnose a deliberately broken local web application without guessing.
steps: Start a tiny server and confirm the exact process and port it uses.
Open the URL in the browser and write down the request/response you expect.
Change the configured port without updating the browser URL and capture the failure.
Use `netstat`, `Get-NetTCPConnection`, or an equivalent tool to identify the listening process.
Break PATH for one terminal session or invoke a missing command; explain why the shell cannot find it.
Add one environment variable, read it at runtime, then compare runtime configuration with build-time configuration.
Write a one-page boundary map: shell → process → port → HTTP → browser.
Reset everything and reproduce the healthy path from memory.
evidence: A clean Git diff or file-tree change
Browser, HTTP, database, test, container, or CI evidence that proves the behavior
One deliberate failure, the evidence you used, and the root-cause fix
A short explanation of why the final responsibility lives in the chosen layer
completion: I can reproduce one key part without the walkthrough.
I can explain one trade-off I deliberately chose.
I can show one failure that my tests, constraints, or runbook now protects against.
